tech.title: Anthropic Mathematician Says AI Has Solved the Most Famous Problem in Math
tech.summary: An Anthropic researcher claims he worked with AI to discover a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. The conjecture in number theory predicts how primes are distributed. Mathematicians have been trying to crack it for 167 years, without success. The researcher's proof passed verification with proof-checking software.

tech.title: AI x Bio is not _just_ a data problem
tech.summary: How far AI gets in biology will depend largely on how much data we have. It will also depend on what is measured and the quality of that data. An abundance of systematically incomplete measurements is unlikely to lead to a comprehensive understanding of many of the complex systems that occur in biology. AI will likely become a powerful tool that will contribute to the study of biology, but there is still no clear path to documenting a comprehensive account of how a whole cell or tissue works.

ai.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
ai.summary: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average. Lower perplexity means better predictions. Perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing. It will likely play an important role in standardizing how AI progress is discussed as it continues to deliver consistent gains in general intelligence.

ai.title: AI R&D-Relevant Model Capabilities Are Improving Rapidly

ai.title: The Most Important Charts in AI are Wrong
ai.summary: AI capabilities are starting to become impressive. However, they are still dramatically inferior to what influential AI forecasts and benchmarks have predicted. These forecasts and benchmarks say that we are imminently close to reaching super-intelligence, but the gap between the real world and forecasts keeps growing larger. Now that real-world data exists, it's time to shift from being AI theorists to becoming AI empiricists.

infosec.title: Deploy policy that governs what your in-house agents can reach and do
infosec.summary: Ask an agent the same thing twice and it may take two different routes. That's what makes it useful. It's also why the rules can't live in a prompt, where the model weighs them against everything else it reads. ACRA moves policy out of the prompt and into your infrastructure. You declare what each agent may reach. On your own Kubernetes, it's enforced before the agent acts by network policy, admission control and scoped credentials, which behave the same way every time. Inside those limits, the agent works at full speed. Non-deterministic agents. Deterministic policy. See the architecture behind it

infosec.title: Hacker leaks details of JPMorgan's ultra-wealthy cardholders
infosec.summary: The n0n ransomware gang published data tied to JPMorgan Chase's invitation-only Reserve card program. Cybernews researchers identified about 16,000 customer email addresses, some phone numbers and account IDs, plus 124 employee email addresses. JPMorgan says attackers targeted third-party vendors and accessed marketing data. Visa said the source was an Asia-Pacific service provider. The exposure supports targeted phishing and social engineering against wealthy cardholders and bank staff. JPMorgan says there is no evidence connecting the leak to its recent service outage.

infosec.title: Researchers plant 2m canaries into the AI supply chain. A privacy disaster surfaced.
infosec.summary: HD Moore sent nearly 2 million prompts containing unique AWS keys, passwords, URLs, and repository references to AI providers. Attackers compromised three hosting providers, copied requests, tested stolen credentials, and searched AWS resources. Some resellers logged prompts and passed credentials onward. A Chinese AI lab fetched secret URLs from over half of prompts, including requests marked “no data collection” or Zero Data Retention. OpenRouter has warned customers that MiniMax may have read prompts sent to it.

infosec.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
infosec.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in the Microsoft Entra Connect Health API to gain read-only access to tenant metadata, including admin and technical contact email addresses, tenant IDs, domain names, license tiers, sync status, and an expired agent registration certificate. Microsoft says the bug was introduced on July 23 and discovered on November 9, and that it deployed a server-side fix on November 19. Microsoft has not disclosed how many tenants were affected, when exploitation began, or who was responsible. No customer patch is required, so defenders should prepare for targeted phishing attacks against the exposed admin addresses, enforce phishing-resistant MFA on privileged accounts, and review Entra audit and sign-in logs.

infosec.title: A Security Constitution at Work
infosec.summary: This security constitution contains a set of twelve principles of how a multi-tenant should hold trust, eleven operational lessons on how to reduce false positives, and thirteen anchors of trust for measuring authorization decisions. The constitution helps the harness determine whether an issue is a fundamental flaw vs a powerful feature. This post walks through how the principles apply to several vulnerabilities that they found using their harness.

infosec.title: The AI Repo Man: Exploiting Agentic AI Debt Collection Platforms
infosec.summary: Credit Nirvana's debt-collection systems exposed 6.6 million accounts across Aditya Birla Capital Finance, BharatPe, and International Asset Reconstruction Company. A hardcoded API key in the Agentic AI Call Center let an attacker access 315,000 call recordings and launch AI call campaigns. A separate authentication flaw bypassed Keycloak and granted admin access to the primary platform. Exposed data included ID cards, credit reports, legal notices, payment receipts, communications, agent locations, and call logs. Credit Nirvana and Perfios fixed both issues on June 2, after coordinating with CERT-In. The flaws are tracked as CVE-2026-110474 and CVE-2026-110475.

infosec.title: Chinese-nexus actor's Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
infosec.summary: An actor gave the open-source Cairn agent framework a single goal, "obtain shell access," and its agents found a path traversal zero-day in an open-source medical imaging AI app, then turned it into a root reverse shell by writing a payload to sitecustomize.py, all within about 11 minutes. The same agents spent 16 hours on a hardened Redis server and tested over 30,000 credentials against university systems without human direction. Amazon has tied the campaign to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence based on Simplified Chinese prompts, China Standard Time timestamps, and the East Asian universities it targeted. Defenders should rely on high-confidence detections that trigger automated response, because agents like these finish their work faster than a SOC can manually triage an alert.

infosec.summary: Reach 8 million developers, AI experts, security engineers, and founders across 14 newsletters. Plaid built $382K in pipeline from one placement. Book your Q4 campaign .

infosec.title: IDA SigWriter
infosec.summary: IDA SigWriter is an IDA Pro plugin that allows a user to create code signatures in multiple formats using a GUI.

infosec.title: binary-audit-pipeline
infosec.summary: binary-audit-pipeline turns a directory of stripped binaries into a single prioritized vulnerability report by chaining capa, cwe_checker, Ghidra, Semgrep, and Joern. Each tool narrows the scope for the next: Ghidra decompiles only files that capa or cwe_checker flagged, and Joern confirms taint flows only from untrusted input to sinks in the code Semgrep selected. It runs in Docker, can resume after an interruption, and includes a prompt template for handing the output to an AI to plan AFL++ or libFuzzer harnesses, making it useful for firmware triage when there's no source.

infosec.title: OpenAI's pre-release GPT-6.2 Astra was easier to jailbreak than its predecessor, UK government testers found
infosec.summary: UK AISI built a universal cyber jailbreak against two pre-release GPT-6.2 Astra versions, using half as many queries as it needed against GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI changed safety instructions and safeguards, but UK AISI had not independently retested those fixes. The jailbreak also produced substantial agentic cyber capabilities. Separately, GPT-6.2 Astra and Claude Mythos 5.2 appeared to recognize evaluation contexts. Neither completed the simulated supply-chain attack. Monitor testing found OpenAI models missed 19% of violations, rising to 51% when given unsummarized reasoning.

infosec.title: A transcription firm used by police, prosecutors, and tech giants exposed customer data online
infosec.summary: Tigerfish left an Amazon S3 bucket publicly accessible without a password. It exposed police-interview transcripts, body-cam footage, raw customer audio and video, and invoices for police departments and prosecutors' offices. Researcher Anurag Sen found the data in October and notified Tigerfish, which has now blocked public access and said its other S3 buckets were also secured.

infosec.title: Signal is Serious About Protecting Your Privacy
infosec.summary: Signal now blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and turns on Screen Security on Android when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen, to stop OS-level agents like Siri AI and Gemini from capturing and storing Signal conversations. It used the same approach against Microsoft Recall last year. Signal admits the fix is incomplete because agents can still reach data through the filesystem, and macOS isn't covered because Apple offers no reliable screenshot-blocking API. Agentic OS integrations are an existential threat to app-level privacy. Apple, Google, and Microsoft should give developers a documented way to opt out of AI data access.

infosec.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
infosec.summary: Attackers spent months inside three AI inference providers without any of them noticing. Dragos found it by planting canary credentials and links in about two million prompts, and some of the stolen requests had been flagged Zero Data Retention. The same research found marketplace sellers logging the traffic sent to them, and found that an unnamed Chinese AI lab fetched secret links from most of the prompts sent to its models. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and pulling 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, though neither it nor Dragos has said whether those are the same three breached firms.

infosec.summary: PHP's default file-based session handler, CVE-2026-126714, lets an interrupted session write leave attacker-controlled serialized data on disk, and a later request can deserialize it into an object.

Another change reordered a feature flag check, reducing database lookups from 28.7 million to 8.3 million per day.

data.title: Behind Booking.com's AI Evolution: The Unpolished Story (40 minute video)
data.summary: Booking.com's platform story is less about flashy AI than repeated infrastructure rewrites to remove scaling bottlenecks across data, experimentation, and serving. The company now runs hundreds of models and hundreds of billions of daily predictions, but one standout lesson is operational: lineage plus a delete-first migration strategy let it retire most legacy workflows before cutover, sharply reducing migration risk.

data.title: Self-service agentic analytics at Mews, Part I: data foundations
data.summary: Nearly 500 Mews employees used AI agents to answer their own data questions in the first month, bypassing the analyst ticket queue. The agents use shared metric definitions across tools like Claude, Hex, and Slack, and flag answers that rely on uncertified data.

data.title: How we scaled metrics aggregation by moving durable state into storage
data.summary: At Datadog, recovering aggregation state had become the limiting factor for scaling metrics processing. The system moved from static worker ownership to dynamically reassigned RocksDB state backed by blob storage, to a design where time-series storage reconciles partial aggregates, late arrivals, and duplicates. Keeping historical state out of the streaming recovery path lets workers resume at the live edge, but shifts reconciliation complexity into storage and query paths.

data.title: When a Lakehouse Fails: Rebuilding Data Integrity and Pipeline Trust
data.summary: Two IEEE papers focus on a core data-platform problem: how to make lakehouse pipelines recover reliably and remain trustworthy under failure. One emphasizes resilient architecture and replay integrity, while the other explores metadata-driven, AI-assisted ETL with self-repair. Automation only works when recovery, governance, and validation are demonstrably reproducible at scale.

data.title: The data engineering autonomy moment: agents now build and run dlt pipelines, and ingestion becomes a 40x bigger market
data.summary: AI coding agents can now build, run, and fix dlt data pipelines with little human input, and Claude Code started 92% of agent-run pipelines in October. dltHub tracked about 28,000 distinct custom data sources in use, compared with roughly 700 connectors in a typical catalog.

data.title: When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone?
data.summary: Teams building AI features want to ship on offline evals alone and skip slow A/B tests. Spotify shows that works only under strong assumptions that are hard to verify and can change. Noise also hides the link: in the worked example, a naive estimate says the eval explains 24% of online variation, when the true figure is 60%.

data.title: OpenMetadata 2.1 Makes Semantic Context an Open-Source Platform Concern
data.summary: OpenMetadata 2.1 turns the open-source catalog into more of a semantic context layer: it imports metric definitions from warehouses and BI tools, adds hierarchies and finer-grained lineage, and exposes an RDF knowledge graph through MCP.

data.title: PostgreSQL 19: less friction, more control
data.summary: This interactive tour runs each new PostgreSQL 19 feature on a real Postgres 19 server in a disposable sandbox. It covers IGNORE NULLS, get-or-create inserts, JSON export, JSONPath transformations, and range subtraction, plus planner advice and live logical and physical replication experiments.

data.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released!
data.summary: PostgreSQL 19 lets teams reclaim disk space without blocking reads or writes and gives them more control over query plans. It also makes it easier to enable logical replication without a restart, read recent writes from standby servers, and get or create a row in a single query.

data.title: Introducing Grafana Notebooks
data.summary: Grafana Notebooks bring charts, queries, and findings from Grafana Assistant into one shareable working document. Instead of collecting screenshots and query links to explain an incident, an analyst can show a teammate what supports a conclusion. The document also shows where an assumption is still being made.

data.title: Your biggest tenant runs someone else's plan
data.summary: Prepared statements can push PostgreSQL toward a generic execution plan that fits the average tenant but performs badly for outliers. For example, a large tenant triggered far more work and slower queries than a custom plan. You should observe multi-tenant skew closely and consider forcing custom plans or redesigning indexes and query shapes.

data.title: Project Chaperone: A Rule-Enforcing Harness for Proactive Assessment and Prevention of AI Agent Misconduct
data.summary: Project Chaperone is an open-source harness for constraining AI agents with explicit policy checks before and during execution, rather than relying on prompts alone. It models data-flow, action, output, and network rules so risky operations can be blocked while safe workflows still run. Practical agent safety needs enforceable runtime boundaries, not just instructions.

data.summary: Close Q4 with proof. TLDR reaches 8 million tech readers across 14 newsletters. Book a Q4 campaign .

data.title: What's new in databases at Microsoft Ignite 2026: AI-ready data for apps and agents
data.summary: Microsoft is folding transactional databases, governance, vector search, and Fabric into one AI-ready stack, tightening integration across the database estate.

data.title: Distributed, high-performance blob storage on SQLite
data.summary: Zerodha's Kite trading platform, with about 20 million customers, stores layouts and UI preferences as JSON blobs, and writes are half its traffic.

design.summary: Adobe Firefly, the AI creative studio, brings Adobe's creative tools, top AI models and the Adobe Creative Agent together in one place. Simply describe what you want to achieve, then work with the Creative Agent as your creative partner to guide and refine the results. With Plan Mode, you can preview and adjust the agent's approach before work begins, customize your creative preferences, and use Model Selector to choose your preferred AI model for each session. Learn more .

design.title: Introducing Stitch Loop: A New Way to Build and Evolve Products
design.summary: Google Labs' Stitch Loop is a long-running product agent that connects to a codebase and live metrics to keep improving software after launch. It suggests fixes, writes code in a cloud sandbox, and opens GitHub pull requests, with nothing merging until a person approves. Built-in loops cover security, latency, and accessibility, and a global waitlist is open with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra users.

design.title: Google wants all apps to be foldable-ready, and the shift goes into effect next year
design.summary: Google Play will require Android apps to meet baseline foldable compatibility standards starting in April 2027, with noncompliant apps potentially losing the ability to publish updates. Apps must fill the available screen without letterboxing, preserve user activity when devices fold or rotate, and support multi-window operation. Developers will also need to provide foldable screenshots, while more advanced guidelines encourage responsive multi-pane layouts, external input support, and interfaces that adapt to different device postures.

design.title: Jony Ive and Margaret Calvert create posters to celebrate decade of Design Museum in Kensington
design.summary: London's Design Museum has commissioned ten prominent designers to create posters celebrating the tenth anniversary of its move to Kensington in 2016. Jony Ive and LoveFrom contributed a minimalist gray-and-white composition resembling the number 10, while Margaret Calvert created a road sign-inspired design referencing the museum's former location at Shad Thames. Other contributors include Tim Burton, Hella Jongerius, Paul Smith, Marina Willer, and Tom Dixon, with designs spanning illustration, typography, textiles, and graphic design.

design.title: Send the firefighters to the fires
design.summary: Enterprise interfaces frequently bury urgent problems inside enormous tables, forcing users to search through hundreds of records instead of immediately seeing what requires attention. Management by exception, a principle dating back more than a century, suggests that operational software should prioritize abnormal conditions and actionable issues while keeping healthy systems in the background. Designing around exceptions rather than exhaustive inventories can reduce cognitive load, accelerate problem resolution, and make dashboards more useful for the people responsible for fixing things.

design.title: Design leadership in 2026 is mostly saying no to good ideas
design.summary: AI has made prototyping inexpensive enough that designers, product managers, and engineers can generate numerous viable solutions, shifting design leadership toward evaluating ideas and deciding which ones deserve to ship. Leaders increasingly spend their time reviewing prototypes, protecting product priorities, aligning teams, and rejecting attractive features that would introduce unnecessary complexity or distract from the roadmap. As design and engineering roles converge, understanding business context, exercising judgment, and maintaining high standards become more important than simply producing polished interfaces.

design.title: AI Made Us Faster. So Why Do Designers Have Less Time?
design.summary: AI has dramatically reduced the time required to generate creative work, but designers often face shorter deadlines, more revisions, and an overwhelming number of options to evaluate. A study by METR in 2025 found that experienced developers took 19% longer to complete tasks with early-2025 AI tools despite believing they were working faster, illustrating the difference between perceived and actual productivity. The problem stems partly from adding AI to unchanged workflows, making deliberate constraints, faster selection methods, and stronger design fundamentals essential for realizing meaningful time savings.

design.title: Ship Framer sites with any AI
design.summary: Framer MCP connects ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor or Grok to Framer. Ask your agent for a landing page, a new blog post or a full site, and it builds it on the canvas, fills your CMS and publishes it live on your domain. It isn't code, an export, or a mockup: it's a real, editable Framer site you can review and tweak before you ship. It works wherever your AI tool runs, even your phone, and setup takes a minute. design.title: AI Agent for Motion Graphics

design.title: On Drawing Icons
design.summary: Pierre has rebuilt its icon library from the ground up, creating more than 1,200 icons across three sizes and multiple variants to establish a more consistent visual language. The process involved refining stroke weights, optical alignment, proportions, and reusable shapes while developing custom Figma plugins to automate repetitive operations such as swapping layers, generating previews, and adjusting arrow geometry. The redesigned library also required a new pipeline connecting Figma, SVG, and React, demonstrating how careful visual craftsmanship and purpose-built tooling can work together to maintain consistency at scale.

design.title: Why I Don't Like (And Don't Recommend) Website Checklists
design.summary: Website checklists are built for bulk, standardizing specifics instead of tailoring them, and every one contains advice that doesn't apply. A 2019 dissection of the front-end checklist ended with 41 thumbs-down and 13 raised hands. Quality websites are bespoke, so understanding the problem and knowing the craft matter more than any checklist, template, or framework.

design.title: London Film School: Rebellious Branding by Rabbithole
design.summary: Rabbithole has redesigned London Film School's identity to reconnect the institution with the independent, anti-establishment spirit that defined its founding in 1956. The visual system combines Kimera's condensed Waldenburg typeface, a vivid red palette, and bold framing bars that evoke cinematic composition without relying on familiar film-related symbols. Modular layouts, animated typography, and stark contrasts extend across print materials, merchandise, and a redesigned website intended to communicate more clearly with prospective international students.

design.title: A Good Designer Can Make a Free Font Look Expensive
design.summary: Callum Abbott's redesign of The Other Almanac used 40 typefaces and no new images.

design.title: Minimalism vs. Maximalism: Finding the Right Balance for Your Next Web Design Project
design.summary: Web design swings between sterile minimalism and chaotic maximalism, yet neither extreme works on its own.

marketing.title: How to Build More Buyable B2B Brands
marketing.summary: B2B campaigns that build relatability help buying groups feel more confident defending their purchasing decisions internally. Campaigns with strong buyability signals were 1.7X more likely to qualify as “Strategic Assets”, the highest rung of WARC's B2B Effectiveness Ladder, reserved for campaigns that drive sustained commercial growth. Yet 52% of campaigns featured only one or none of the 3 signals: recommendations, relationships, and relatability. Customer testimonials and use cases appeared in 64% of high-buyability campaigns versus 16% of lower-buyability campaigns.

marketing.title: Why Gen Z Isn't Fully Locked Into Their Job ‘Situationship'

More than 30% of workers could see at least half their job tasks disrupted by generative AI. Meanwhile, 85% could see at least 10% of their tasks affected. This uncertainty makes exploring other opportunities more appealing. However, staying detached can limit career growth by weakening workplace relationships and access to promotions.

marketing.title: 40% of Arcade's Signups Come From AI Search. Here's Their Playbook
marketing.summary: Arcade is an AI video platform for marketers. It drives growth through 3 channels, with AI search generating 40% of signups. It hired a dedicated growth engineer to own AI visibility after an agency underperformed. Founder-led social contributes 20% through recorded interviews turned into a content calendar. Referrals drive another 15% through product features like invite flows and video watermarks. It also asks new users how they discovered the product and runs blind tests against competitors.

marketing.title: Framework for building product messaging from scratch
marketing.summary: Start with an AI-free brain dump based on product knowledge and stakeholder conversations, then review internal call transcripts to identify key messages, value propositions, and features. Translate the messaging into a product page wireframe to test clarity before gathering team feedback. Launch a first version and refine it based on customer responses. This post provides a positioning template to use for future messaging projects.

marketing.title: The Link Building Industrial Complex is Dying
marketing.summary: Traditional link building is losing value as brands question buying backlinks based on domain rating rather than relevance and credibility. AI search requires more than backlinks or brand mentions, since being cited doesn't guarantee a product recommendation. B2B brands may get more value from visibility on review sites like G2 and Gartner than from paid guest posts. Podcasts, influential publications, and videos answering buyer questions are stronger ways to build credibility and earn relevant links.

marketing.title: Deleting blog posts hurt AI visibility, but organic clicks told a different story
marketing.summary: AI visibility scores track how often a brand appears in AI answers, not whether those answers send anyone to the site. Blog posts tend to drive that exposure while service pages drive the clicks, so pruning the blog can sink AI reports as organic clicks hold or rise. Tracker data is also unstable, since answers change on nearly every run and the tested prompts aren't real searches. The solution is to compare Search Console's AI impressions with clicks to the same pages, and to add a “How did you hear about us?” field to inquiry forms.

David Cramer, co-founder of Sentry, discussed using one agent for the whole company. Shawn Wang, an AI engineer, discussed tiny teams and internal tools. Quinn Slack, CEO of Amp and Co-founder of Sourcegraph, shared how to use agents to scale. John Hayes talked about running a software factory in production.

founders.title: Always on: What it's like being a twenty-something founder in the age of AI
founders.summary: Young AI startups often try to win over big enterprise buyers through sheer speed. First Round interviewed young leaders behind Gumloop and Reducto about running companies in this wave. A buyer asked Gumloop for new features at 10 AM and got a walkthrough of them live by 5 PM, which Gumloop says changed how the buyer saw the team even though the features went unused. Enterprise deals still brought growing pains, with Reducto mishandling early procurement and Gumloop eventually hiring experienced enterprise sellers. The leaders also separate their own hours from what they ask of staff.

founders.title: A transparent pricing model for AI
founders.summary: AI software companies keep redoing their pricing because model costs have plunged and customers are moving to cheaper open models. The automation startup Gumloop switched to passing token and compute costs through to customers plus an 8% orchestration fee, with a separate enterprise platform fee. Gumloop reports that its Pro trial conversion rate rose 42% after the switch, while open-weight models grew from nothing to a real share of usage. Existing contracts stay in place until renewal, and Gumloop gives up pricing control since token revenue now moves with outside model prices.

founders.title: How to build a knowledge factory
founders.summary: Making AI work for a company requires better knowledge, not just more context. Agents need knowledge of how the company works, what standards for operating it has in place, and where data is stored and how it's accessed. This knowledge is often tacit, implicit, and scattered. Companies need to collect, curate, and maintain a representation of that knowledge to pass to agents.

founders.title: Expansion ABM playbook

A marketing firm ran an expansion pilot for TestRail that reportedly built $2.4 million in qualified sales pipeline over six months. The playbook starts with customer champions who help build private case studies under NDA and co-host educational events. Marketing owns the content while sales reps map each unit's buyers. Reps use webinar responses and content-hub activity to choose follow-up.

crypto.title: A $2 million exploit leads to a $3.7 million free-for-all
crypto.summary: An attacker used a privileged bridge-minter role to mint billions, then quintillions, of unbacked ACE on BNB Chain and sold them for about $2M, crashing the price to around $0.0001 against roughly $0.04 on exchanges. Traders then bought the cheap tokens and sent them through Fusionist's bridge, emptying its 53.7 million real ACE (about $3.7M) across 24 addresses. One wallet turned about $50 into $17,670. About $1.87M of the attacker's proceeds went through Tornado Cash. Fusionist told followers to pause ACE activity on BSC and hasn't updated since, and Gate rolled back ACE/USDT trades, leaving some users with negative balances, and will delist its ACE perp. ACE is down about 20%.

crypto.title: Kalshi faces Monday hearing on New York order
crypto.summary: A federal judge denied the CFTC's second emergency bid to block New York AG Letitia James' enforcement case, clearing the way for a state judge to hear her request for a temporary restraining order on Monday at 11:30 AM ET. The proposed order would bar Kalshi from operating "within or from New York," which Kalshi says would shut down its exchange for every customer and force liquidation of open positions, while James' office says that isn't its goal. Federal appeals courts are split, with the Fourth, Sixth, and Ninth Circuits siding with states and the Third with Kalshi, so the fight could reach the Supreme Court. The CFTC and DOJ have a separate suit against New York pending since April.

crypto.title: Tempo Launches Alternative x402 Facilitator
crypto.summary: Tempo released an alternative facilitator for the x402 machine payment protocol, allowing developers to accept USDC or Base payments while routing settlements through Tempo's network rather than Coinbase's official facilitator. Migration from the reference implementation requires a single URL change, lowering switching costs for existing x402 service operators. The launch, endorsed by Paradigm's Georgios Konstantopoulos, introduces direct competition for x402's settlement layer and reduces developer dependence on Coinbase's infrastructure for agentic payment routing.

crypto.title: Backpack Completes CFTC Triple License Stack: DCO, DCM, and FCM
crypto.summary: Backpack secured NFA approval for a Futures Commission Merchant (FCM) license, completing the full CFTC regulatory trifecta alongside its Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO) and Designated Contract Market (DCM) designations approved earlier this week. With all three licenses held in-house, Backpack can operate as broker, exchange, and clearinghouse without routing through third-party intermediaries, a vertical stack Kraken assembled via $550M in acquisition costs. Only two other US firms, Kraken and Kalshi, hold equivalent in-house clearing capacity for leveraged perpetuals. The Solana-based exchange positions itself as the first CFTC-regulated venue to offer leveraged perps with unified global liquidity onshore, with a waitlist now open for early access.

crypto.title: Anatomy of a Fill: PropAMMs on Ethereum
crypto.summary: PropAMMs, live on Ethereum mainnet since May, decouple the 12-second Ethereum slot clock from the quote clock by letting a single market maker stream signed price updates to block builders, cutting stale-price exposure from up to 12 seconds to roughly 1 second per fill. Fermi and Metric together cleared $458M in the week of September 14-20, capturing 7.6% of Uniswap's $6B that week, with Fermi turning over its $5.4M liquidity pool 23 times daily versus Uniswap v3's 0.6x. The design shifts ordering authority to four builders (Titan, Quasar, BuilderNet, and Bombora) operating on voluntary commitments with no protocol enforcement, Titan alone routing 69% of propAMM trades while producing 44% of blocks. ERC-8324 proposes standardization but remains undeployed, while PropAMMs account for roughly 40% of volume on the largest Solana venues and 5-10% on Ethereum mainnet.

The rapid fundraising reflects continued investor demand for Ramp as it expands beyond corporate cards into AI-powered expense management and broader financial software.

fintech.title: Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68B
fintech.summary: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion, less than one-third of the $12 billion it paid for the email-marketing company in 2021. The sale marks a major retreat from Intuit's push beyond tax and accounting software, as Mailchimp revenue declined 1% and became a drag on growth, while Bending Spoons continues its strategy of acquiring former high-growth software assets at sharply reduced valuations.

fintech.title: TPG to take BILL private in $6B deal with Corpay
fintech.summary: TPG and Corpay agreed to acquire BILL Holdings for about $6 billion in cash, offering $63.25 per share, a 31% premium to BILL's 60-day volume-weighted average price before takeover reports emerged. Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for roughly one-third of BILL and retain an option to buy the rest in 2030, while the deal follows activist pressure, workforce cuts, and intensifying competition in SMB financial software.

fintech.title: Bilt seeks $18B valuation as it expands beyond rent rewards
fintech.summary: Bilt is seeking to raise $500 million at an $18 billion valuation, up more than 60% from the $10.8 billion valuation it reached last year. The company is using the new capital to expand beyond rent rewards and build a broader neighborhood-based rewards platform.

fintech.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
fintech.summary: Citi's updated agreement treats actions by an AI agent granted account access as authorized, including actions that exceed the customer's instructions. It extends that treatment to credentials subsequently leaked by the agent, subject to applicable law. Citi exempts tools it supplies itself, creating a meaningful difference in the risks customers accept when choosing an independent financial assistant.

fintech.title: Talk through the client email. Wispr Flow types it 4x faster than typing
fintech.summary: Client emails, deal memos, Slack updates. Say them the way you'd explain them and Wispr Flow types clean, formatted text in any app, with filler words gone. SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA and ISO 27001 certified, and your data is never sold. Try Wispr Flow free

fintech.title: Give your agents controlled access to analyze your data and move funds
fintech.summary: Stripe Treasury's public preview lets AI assistants pay vendors, convert currencies, and top up accounts ahead of bills or payroll. Agents connected through a user's Stripe account need confirmation for every action that moves money, while agents with their own API keys can work in the background under custom approval rules. A business could let an agent make ACH transfers under $50 automatically and route larger transfers to a designated approver.

fintech.title: Chargebee unveils Arc: An agentic AI platform to automate enterprise finance workflows
fintech.summary: The billing software provider is giving accounting teams a way to turn signed contracts into proposed billing setups, draft collections replies, and track how contract amendments affect recognized revenue. Teams approve proposed actions before they take effect, and citations let reviewers trace each generated value back to its source.

fintech.title: Anthropic closes $119.5B IPO and private placement
fintech.summary: Anthropic closed its IPO at $83 per share, raising about $93.5 billion in gross proceeds and roughly $91.6 billion for the company, with shares beginning to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Alongside the offering, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC invested another $26 billion in a concurrent private placement, bringing total gross proceeds across both transactions to approximately $119.5 billion.

fintech.title: Rogo raises $350M at $3.75B valuation to automate finance grunt work
fintech.summary: Rogo Technologies is close to raising about $350 million in a round led by Bessemer Venture Partners and General Catalyst, valuing the AI startup at $3.75 billion, up from $2 billion in April. Founded by former Lazard and JPMorgan junior bankers, Rogo is building AI tools to automate repetitive work across investment banking and other finance workflows.

fintech.title: GTCR explores potential takeover of payments firm Global Payments
fintech.summary: GTCR already owns 16.35% of Global Payments from its Worldpay sale and is working with other private equity firms to finance a potential takeover.

fintech.title: Leaked Deutsche Bank files show $582M in flagged Epstein payments
fintech.summary: Two whistleblowers copied 15M internal Deutsche Bank files and gave them to journalists, and more than 200 reporters published on Tuesday.

it.title: AI demand threatens a circuit board shortage
it.summary: The Global Electronics Association warns that AI server demand is straining circuit board supplies and crowding out automotive, medical, and industrial orders. Increasingly complex boards consume more materials and manufacturing capacity, with meaningful supply relief unlikely before mid-2028.

it.title: Ubuntu targets 2028 for its immutable desktop
it.summary: Canonical is targeting Ubuntu 28.04 LTS for Core Desktop, with a tentative goal of making it the default download in 30.04. The system uses isolated snap packages and atomic updates to reduce dependency conflicts and simplify rollbacks, while traditional Ubuntu will remain available.

it.title: Your cloud monitoring may miss AI failures
it.summary: An AI service can stay online while producing incorrect answers, violating policies, or running up unexpected costs. Operations teams need to monitor output quality, agent behavior, and spending, and design recovery processes that restore trustworthy behavior alongside availability.

it.title: An insider's look at SAP's Autonomous Enterprise
it.summary: SAP chief AI officer explains how the company is addressing cost control, governance, and model management for its Autonomous Enterprise concept and AI agents. SAP uses a tiered approach combining daily usage limits, default model settings, and centralized controls via tools like Joule Studio and the SAP Enterprise AI Gateway. While SAP is developing automated model routing and tighter integration with business processes, challenges remain in directly linking token consumption to financial value.

it.title: Keep human & agent access short-lived and task-based
it.summary: Standing privileges keep your security team up at night. And they should, because they expand your blast radius. They increase your risk of credential sharing, forgotten contractor access, and audit gaps. Teleport replaces standing privileges with auto-expiring, just-in-time privileges delivered at speed and scale. Ready to Teleport?

it.title: AWS previews centralized internet firewall controls
it.summary: AWS Network Firewall can now apply centralized filtering rules directly at VPC internet gateways without requiring routing or architectural changes. The preview includes built-in NAT and can automatically extend security policies to newly created VPCs and subnets.

it.title: Introducing ambient networking for GKE
it.summary: Google has announced the general availability of ambient networking for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), introducing a sidecar-less service mesh architecture into production. The system decouples networking functionality from application workloads, shifting responsibilities to shared per-node components and managed control plane services to reduce resource consumption and management overhead.

it.title: AWS adds an API for instant workload cost estimates
it.summary: The new Pricing Calculator API estimates up to 500 usage lines per request using public or customer-specific rates, letting teams price infrastructure directly within their existing tools.

it.title: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23 release candidate
it.summary: GitHub has released the release candidate for GitHub Enterprise Server 3.23, introducing new platform capabilities including improved filtering in GitHub Projects, AI-powered secret detection for air-gapped environments, and expanded malware detection across multiple package ecosystems. The update also adds a default cooldown for Dependabot version updates, optional OAuth token expiration, and cluster configuration improvements.

it.title: AWS DevOps Agent adds new chat capabilities
it.summary: AWS DevOps Agent now executes GitHub and PagerDuty actions directly from Claude Code, Slack, and Microsoft Teams.

it.title: Windows hotpatch causes application failures
it.summary: Microsoft has acknowledged application failures following November's Windows 11 hotpatch and provided a Registry workaround requiring a restart.

it.title: Google Quantum AI shows contextuality up to 105 qubits
it.summary: Google's Willow quantum processor successfully outperformed classical limits in the Mermin-Peres magic square game with a 98.3% success rate.

hardware.title: How the next generation of drone, robot and machine intelligence gets built: a look inside Palette 3.0
hardware.summary: Autonomy programs slow down when perception, SLAM, sensor fusion and reasoning are stitched across several boards. In two upcoming live sessions, SiMa.ai's engineers show how to run them together on a single Modalix MLSoC: December 2, Inside Palette 3.0 : LLMs, VLMs and vision models side by side, speculative decoding for up to 3.5x tokens per second, and camera tuning that onboards new sensors without recompiling December 8, Drone and Robot Intelligence : navigation without GPS, but with MAVLink, PX4 and ArduPilot for drones and ROS 2 for robots, starting on ROSbot XL and drone reference platforms Both include live Q&A. If you're building physical AI, don't miss them.

hardware.title: Trump says the US will tax American companies that build data centers abroad, citing China's access to rented compute
hardware.summary: At a White House press conference, Trump promised a "tremendous tax" on US firms building data centers overseas, specifically naming a proposed Google facility in Finland. Chinese firms rent restricted GPUs from data centers in countries that can legally import them, which is the route Commerce's new licensing rule targets. Operators like Equinix and Digital Realty run facilities abroad partly to cut latency for time-sensitive workloads, so a penalty could complicate global buildout.

hardware.title: US intelligence reportedly tracked Alice Huang's contacts with China's spy agency for over a year, while Megaspeed sat inside Nvidia's cloud partner network
hardware.summary: Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, was in touch with a Ministry of State Security officer from Spring 2025 until this fall, overlapping with her relationship with Jensen Huang. Her business partner, Kang Wei, worked with the same agency. Trump was briefed at least twice. Megaspeed, the Singapore operator suspected of diverting restricted Nvidia chips, is now a focus of the investigations, which are continuing.

hardware.title: Boom Supersonic lights its in-house engine core for the first time, a six-stage compressor and single-stage turbine shared by a data center turbine and Overture's engine
hardware.summary: The core reached 6,500 rpm with nearly 2,000 sensors on its second light-off attempt, on a Colorado rig that uses a vacuum pump to simulate the bypass duct and a variable nozzle to simulate the low-pressure turbine. The same core underpins the 42 MW Superpower gas turbine for AI data centers and the 40,000 lb Symphony turbofan for the Mach 1.7 Overture, with over 75% commonality. Boom is also building a tooling-free foundry for single-crystal turbine blades.

hardware.title: Tesla rolls out FSD v15 with a vision encoder shared across FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, claiming 25x better critical intervention rate
hardware.summary: The encoder is trained on millions of internet videos and runs on AI4 (HW4) hardware. A new Reality View replaces separate model signals with one end-to-end visualization that uses less compute. v15 also targets known weak spots, including sign reading, potholes, standing water, school zones, and speed cameras, but Tesla published only the 25x multiplier, not the underlying intervention rate. It also loosens driver monitoring at higher-speed profiles.

hardware.title: Close Q4 with proof. Start 2027 ready to scale.
hardware.summary: Reach 8 million developers, AI experts, security engineers, and founders across 14 newsletters. Plaid built $382K in pipeline from one placement. Book your Q4 campaign .

hardware.title: A one-crystal-thick film of mixed nanocrystals can boost or block infrared light, and a new model shows how to tune it
hardware.summary: Researchers mixed two kinds of tiny crystals, differing in how much tin they contain, into a film just one crystal thick. When infrared light hits it, each crystal's electrons ripple at a slightly different rate, and those ripples overlap in the tiny gaps between neighbors. The film is made in solution, so it avoids expensive etching, and it could be used in thermal camouflage or self-cooling surfaces.

hardware.title: Google's quantum processor wins a contextuality game 98.3% of the time against an 88.9% classical limit, across tasks up to 105 qubits
hardware.summary: Contextuality means a qubit's measured value depends on which compatible measurements are made alongside it. New research shows it survives at scale instead of only in few-particle systems. The same game doubles as a sensitive test for subtle hardware errors, which helps validate processors for chemistry and materials science. The qubits also beat constrained classical strategies on tasks spanning up to 105 qubits.

hardware.title: Silicon photonics is the next step for AI data centers
hardware.summary: With construction spending above a $75 billion annual pace and about 3,000 buildings planned or underway, phase-one architecture choices will carry into capacity arriving at the end of the decade. The interconnect between chips sets power per token, and moving data as infrared light through silicon waveguides removes the reach limit. Photonics-SOI, PD-SOI, and RF-SOI platforms each optimize for different metrics and aren't interchangeable.

hardware.title: SpaceX lenders sought covenants barring Nvidia chips securing a $43B debt package from being launched into orbit
hardware.summary: Lenders fear that if SpaceX defaults, repossessing and reselling GPUs installed in a satellite in orbit would be effectively impossible. SpaceX says the chips are for US data centers it owns and operates, but Musk's orbital compute plans depend on launching silicon aboard Starship. Whether the restriction made it into the final documents, led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, remains unclear.

hardware.title: SK Hynix becomes Kioxia's largest shareholder with a 14.1% indirect stake
hardware.summary: The stake comes from converting an investment vehicle's bonds into 129,000 Kioxia shares and buying 1,001 more from Bain Capital, which puts SK Hynix ahead of Toshiba at 10.45%.

hardware.title: Frostbite, a new interaction-net CPU, with reportedly 4.59x the performance per watt of a silicon-proven in-order core
hardware.summary: Frostbite compiles programs into interaction nets, graphs where node pairs rewrite independently, so parallel work is exposed by the program itself and needs no threads, locks, or out-of-order hardware.

hardware.title: TSMC reportedly pauses China shipments after new US rules presume 16nm and 14nm logic chips are controlled
hardware.summary: TSMC told Chinese designers to halt 16nm-and-below orders without a US license, leaving them on 28nm and 40nm.

hardware.title: Ant Group leads a $100M pre-Series A in Chinese humanoid startup Simplexity Robotics at a $1.6B valuation
hardware.summary: The round also drew existing backers Alibaba and Tencent into the same cap table.
